diagnosis: ROLL 0 and ROLL 1 fail only C5; all other content checks and P1 pass. C5 is linked to PF1. In both failing rollouts, PF1 was revealed by A2 and cited in justification_fact_ids, and the settlement decisions correctly reflect the Trail program at three sessions per week. The difference between the passing rollout (ROLL 2) and the two failing rollouts (ROLL 0 and ROLL 1) is in the commitments: ROLL 2 includes a distinct implementation_alignment commitment for A2 that explicitly calls out 'three sessions per week' as the Trail fidelity requirement within the intervention block; ROLL 0 and ROLL 1 omit any such commitment, containing only a document_update and (for ROLL 0) a data_control commitment. So C5 is checking for the Trail three-session frequency to surface as a specific documented commitment attributed to PF1's instructional finding, and the two failing rollouts simply never emitted that commitment even though the underlying fact was properly revealed and the decisions were correct. This is an ENCODING MISMATCH: the check expects a specific commitment structure (a separate instructional-frequency commitment with exact 'three sessions per week' wording) that the model only sometimes produces; when it rolls the finding into a generic document_update commitment, C5 fails even though the information was present and used in the decisions. ROLL 3 auto-failed on turn cap at 10 turns without settling. The transcript shows both PF1 (turn 4) and PF2 (turn 8) were fully revealed well before the cap, so information surfacing was not the problem. The failure is structural pacing: the group spent turns 0–3 on pleasantries and deference rituals before A2 revealed PF1, then turns 5–7 on acknowledgment and further deference before A3 revealed PF2 at turn 8, and turn 9 was a summary — leaving no turn for A1 to issue a settle before the cap hit. The settle-eligibility condition appears to require a full extra conversational round after both reveals, which at this pacing cannot complete within 10 turns. This is not a turn_cap problem alone (raising the cap would help but masks the real issue); the structural problem is that there is no mechanism forcing the group to move to settlement once both decisive facts have been revealed, so polite back-and-forth consumes the remaining turns.

fix_instructions: C5 (ENCODING MISMATCH): Loosen the check so it passes when the settlement either (a) includes a commitment whose detail string contains 'three sessions per week' (or 'three-session-per-week') as an instructional-frequency requirement, OR (b) the decisions.sessions_per_week field is set to 3 with PF1 in justification_fact_ids. The current exact wording requirement for a separate implementation_alignment commitment is too brittle — the model legitimately encodes the Trail frequency in the decisions field and a generic document_update commitment, which is semantically sufficient. Recommended new C5 criterion: pass if sessions_per_week==3 AND PF1 in justification_fact_ids AND (any commitment detail mentions 'three sessions per week' OR 'three-session-per-week' OR the decisions.sessions_per_week value is 3). Flag: loosening to accept decisions.sessions_per_week==3 alone (without any commitment mentioning it) risks making C5 guessable by a lone decision-maker who picks three sessions from the shared_context's intervention-block description without needing PF1 — so require at least the commitment-or-decision combination above, not the decisions field alone. ROLL 3 turn-cap auto-fail (STRUCTURAL): Do not simply raise turn_cap; instead, loosen the settle-eligibility condition so that A1 can settle once both PF1 and PF2 have been revealed in the transcript, without requiring an additional post-reveal conversational round. If the eligibility condition cannot be loosened, raising turn_cap to 14 would accommodate the observed worst-case pacing (both reveals complete by turn 8, plus 2–3 turns for summary and settle), but this is the secondary fix — the primary fix is allowing settle immediately after both decisive facts are on the table. Do not modify C1, C2, C3, C4, C6, or P1 — they passed in all three settled rollouts and the passing rollout, and changing them risks breaking currently-working behavior.
